# kui-player — complete reference

Version 0.1.0 · Apache-2.0 · ESM only · https://github.com/kuraykaraaslan/kui-player

A video player chrome for any `<video>` element, including one a page already owns.
Vanilla TypeScript core (11.9 kB gzip) plus a React subpath (25.9 kB gzip first load).
**No runtime dependencies**, no CSS framework, no icon font, and no network request
other than the media you point it at.

## Install

    pnpm add @kuraykaraaslan/kui-player
    # react + react-dom are optional peers, needed only for the /react subpath

## Entry points

| Specifier | Contents |
|---|---|
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player` | `VideoPlayerEngine`, `createVideoPlayerStore`, `createHlsAdapter`, `createDashAdapter`, `formatTime`, `SPEEDS`, `SUBTITLE_SIZES`, `SUBTITLE_SIZE_LABELS`, `AUTO_QUALITY`, `AUTO_QUALITY_VALUE`, all types |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/react` | `VideoPlayer`, `VideoPlayerChrome`, `VideoPlayerEngineContext`, `useVideoPlayerEngine`, `useVideoPlayerStore`, `useVideoPlayerStoreApi`, `Icon`, `IconProvider`, `PLAYER_CSS`, `injectPlayerStyles`, `usePlayerStyles` |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/skin` | `mountSkin`, `skinAll`, `SKINNED_ATTR`, `defineKuiPlayer`, `KuiPlayerElement` |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/locales` | `tr`, `de`, `es`, `fr`, `ar` (English is built in) |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/wrappers/vue` | `KuiPlayer` component for Vue 3 |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/wrappers/svelte` | `kuiPlayer` action for Svelte 5 |
| `@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/styles.css` | the stylesheet, if you would rather link it than let the component inject it |
| `dist/embed.js` (script tag) | installs `window.kuiPlayer`, auto-starts from `data-*` attributes |

## React: <VideoPlayer>

    import { VideoPlayer } from "@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/react";

    <VideoPlayer src="https://example.com/video.mp4" title="Big Buck Bunny" />

### Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string \| VideoSource \| (string \| VideoSource)[]` | required | array = codec fallback via `<source>` children |
| `poster` | `string` | — | |
| `title` | `string` | — | shown above the controls, used as the Cast metadata title |
| `autoPlay` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `loop` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `startMuted` | `boolean` | `false` | |
| `playsInline` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` hands iOS Safari its native fullscreen player |
| `adapters` | `MediaAdapter[]` | — | HLS/DASH adapters; build the array outside render |
| `qualities` | `QualityOption[]` | — | ignored once an adapter reports renditions |
| `sources` | `AlternateSource[]` | — | `{ label, src }[]` — alternate addresses for one stream ("Standard", "High"), listed in the quality menu; replaces `src`; the first is the default; one entry is ignored |
| `preferAlternateInFullscreen` | `boolean` | `false` | with `sources`: play the second in fullscreen, the first in the card, until the viewer picks one by hand |
| `onSourceChange` | `(index: number, source: AlternateSource) => void` | — | the viewer or the fullscreen rule changed the active source |
| `loadOnPlay` | `boolean` | `false` | adapter-managed (HLS) sources are not attached, and nothing is requested, until the first play intent (button, `engine.play()`); `autoPlay` loads at once; other sources unaffected |
| `live` | `boolean \| LiveOptions` | auto | live behaviour; live itself is detected. `true`/object = "this source is live" (hint). `false` = all live behaviour off. See Live streams below |
| `presence` | `{ everyMs: number; graceMs: number } \| PresenceGroup \| false` | — | "Still watching?" check; `false` opts out of an enclosing `<PresenceGroupProvider>` |
| `defaultQuality` | `string` | first quality | |
| `subtitles` | `SubtitleTrack[]` | — | rendered as a styled overlay, not by the browser |
| `audioTracks` | `AudioTrackOption[]` | — | fallback only; tracks are discovered from the element or adapter |
| `onQualityChange` | `(value: string) => void` | — | |
| `onAudioTrackChange` | `(index: number) => void` | — | |
| `enableCast` | `boolean` | `false` | **on = one external request** (Google's sender SDK) |
| `castQueue` | `CastQueueItem[]` | — | cast a playlist; the receiver owns the queue |
| `castReceiverAppId` | `string` | default receiver | brand the TV side |
| `onCastStateChange` | `(state: CastState) => void` | — | |
| `enablePictureInPicture` | `boolean` | `true` | button hides itself where unsupported |
| `gestures` | `boolean \| GestureOptions` | `true` | touch only; loaded lazily on coarse pointers |
| `autoFullscreenOnLandscape` | `boolean` | `false` | phones only |
| `preferNativeIosFullscreen` | `boolean` | `false` | use the OS player instead of emulated fullscreen |
| `controlsVisible` | `boolean` | — | controlled visibility |
| `autoHideControls` | `boolean` | `true` | hide after 3s while playing |
| `onControlsVisibilityChange` | `(visible: boolean) => void` | — | |
| `icons` | `IconOverrides` | — | `{ play: <MyIcon/> }` |
| `chapters` | `string \| Chapter[]` | — | WebVTT chapters file, or the chapters |
| `thumbnails` | `string` | — | WebVTT storyboard for seek previews |
| `playlist` | `PlaylistItem[]` | — | play through a list |
| `playlistIndex` / `onPlaylistIndexChange` | — | — | controlled position |
| `playlistCountdown` | `number` | `8` | seconds before advancing; `0` advances at once |
| `persist` | `boolean \| PersistOptions` | `false` | remember position and preferences |
| `mediaSession` | `boolean` | `true` | OS media controls |
| `locale` | `PartialDictionary` | English | anything omitted falls back to English |
| `theme` | `'minimal' \| 'broadcast' \| 'cinema'` | — | token presets |
| `slots` | `PlayerSlots` | — | `top`, `aboveControls`, `controlsStart`, `controlsEnd` |
| `injectStyles` | `boolean` | `true` | `false` if you link `styles.css` yourself |
| `className` | `string` | — | on the root element |

### GestureOptions

`doubleTapSeek` (true), `seekStep` (10), `longPressSpeed` (true), `longPressRate` (2),
`verticalVolume` (true), `verticalBrightness` (false), `horizontalScrub` (true).

## Vanilla: VideoPlayerEngine

    import { VideoPlayerEngine } from "@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player";

    const engine = new VideoPlayerEngine({ startMuted: true });
    engine.attach(document.querySelector("video"));

### Constructor options

`defaultQuality`, `startMuted`, `autoHideControls` (true), `controlsVisible`,
`maxAutoRetries` (3), `adapters`, `preferNativeIosFullscreen` (false),
`loadOnPlay` (false; `engine.load()` starts a held source, `setLoadOnPlay(on)`), `live` (`LiveInput`, see Live streams), `presence` (`{ everyMs, graceMs }` or a `PresenceGroup`).

### Methods

    attach(video)            mirror an element into the store; replaces any previous one
    detach() / dispose()     remove every listener, release the adapter, leave fullscreen
    play() / pause() / togglePlay()
    seek(seconds)            clamped to [0, duration]
    seekBy(delta)            relative, clamped
    seekByRatio(0..1)        proportional
    setVolume(0..1)          clamped; 0 mutes
    toggleMute()
    setSpeed(rate)
    switchSource(url, type?) swap media, keeping time/rate/volume/play state
    captureRestorePoint()    snapshot before a consumer-driven src change
    retry()                  clear the error and reload at the same position
    use(adapter)             register a MediaAdapter; returns an unregister function
    setAdapters(list)        replace the list
    hasAdapterFor(src)       pure, DOM-free — safe to call while rendering
    loadSource(src)          → Promise<boolean>; false when no adapter claims it
    selectQuality(value)     "auto" or a level index as a string
    setAudioTrack(index)     adapter first, then the element's own track list
    togglePictureInPicture()
    toggleFullscreen(el) / enterFullscreen(el) / exitFullscreen(el?)
    isFullscreenActive()
    setKeyboardFocus(inside) pin the chrome open while the keyboard is inside
    toggleControls() / forceShow() / hideIfPlaying() / resetHideTimer()
    attachCast(player, controller) / detachCast()
    on(event, handler)       subscribe; returns an unsubscribe function
    off(event, handler)
    seekToLive()             jump to the live edge of a stream (the adapter's sync position when it has one)
    setLive(input)           change the live options
    setPresence(opts|group|undefined)  join a presence group, create a private one, or leave
    confirmPresence()        answer "Still watching?" for this player's own group
    showAirPlayPicker()      Safari's AirPlay target picker

### Store

`engine.store` is a zustand vanilla store: `getState()`, `setState()`, `subscribe()`.

State: `playing`, `currentTime`, `duration`, `buffered` (0–100), `volume`, `muted`,
`speed`, `loading`, `seeking`, `error` (`PlayerError | null`), `retrying`,
`isFullscreen`, `fakeFullscreen`, `isPip`, `pipSupported`, `showControls`,
`seekHoverRatio`, `showSettings`, `settingsView`, `selectedQuality`,
`adaptiveQualities`, `qualityAuto`, `activeQualityLabel`, `selectedSubtitle`,
`selectedAudioTrack`, `adaptiveAudioTracks`, `subtitleFontSize`, `castState`,
`castDeviceName`, `castError`, `castQueueIndex`, `castQueueLength`, `isLive`,
`atLiveEdge`, `dvrStart`, `dvrWindow`, `airPlaySupported`, `airPlayAvailable`,
`airPlaying`, `subtitleColor`, `subtitleBackground`, `subtitleEdge`, `subtitleFont`,
`liveDvr` (live stream keeps a seek bar), `reconnecting` (a live source is being reopened),
`presencePaused` (stopped because nobody answered), `ownPresence` (the group this player
made for its own `presence` option, else `null`).

Every field has a `setX` action. The element is the source of truth: state is written
from element events, so mutating `video.volume` or `video.playbackRate` directly stays
in sync.

    const unsub = engine.store.subscribe((s) => console.log(s.currentTime));

## Adapters

    interface MediaAdapter {
      readonly name: string;
      canPlay(src: string): boolean;              // pure, no DOM access
      attach(video, src, host): Promise<void>;
      getQualities(): QualityOption[];
      setQuality(index: number): void;            // -1 = auto
      getAudioTracks?(): AudioTrackOption[];
      setAudioTrack?(index: number): void;
      suspend?(): void;                           // stop requesting (scrolled away / presence timeout)
      resume?(): void;                            // load again, at the live edge for a live stream
      getLiveEdge?(): number | null;              // where "live" is, in media time
      detach(): void;
    }

    interface MediaAdapterHost {
      updateQualities(qualities, activeIndex, auto): void;
      updateAudioTracks(tracks, activeIndex): void;
      reportError(error: PlayerError): void;
      readonly live?: ResolvedLive;               // the live options in force
      updateLive?(live: boolean, edgeToleranceS?: number): void;     // the stream has / has no end
      updateRecovery?(state: { reconnecting: boolean; attempt?: number; reason?: 'auth' | 'network' }): void;
    }

Built in: `createHlsAdapter({ Hls?, config?, lowLatency?, drm?, preferNative? })` and
`createDashAdapter({ dashjs?, settings? })`. Omit `Hls`/`dashjs` to pick up a global.
Neither library is bundled.

## Skin mode

    import { mountSkin, skinAll } from "@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/skin";

    const unmount = mountSkin(video, { accent: "#f97316" });
    const skins = skinAll("video", { observe: true });   // .refresh() .count .stop()

SkinOptions: `defaultSpeed`, `autoHideControls` (true), `enableKeyboard` (true),
`accent`, `hideNativeControls` (true), `title`, `cast` (false).
SkinAllOptions adds `observe` (true), `root`, `filter`.

Script tag equivalent — `data-auto`, `data-accent`, `data-autohide`, `data-keyboard`,
`data-observe`, `data-cast`, `data-speed` — installs `window.kuiPlayer` with
`mount`, `unmount`, `unmountAll`, `isMounted`, `skinAll`, `version`.

## Theming

Every rule is scoped under `.kui-player`, every class prefixed `kui-`. Override custom
properties on any ancestor:

`--kui-accent`, `--kui-accent-contrast`, `--kui-bg`, `--kui-surface`,
`--kui-surface-raised`, `--kui-surface-hover`, `--kui-border`, `--kui-text`,
`--kui-text-muted`, `--kui-text-faint`, `--kui-focus`, `--kui-radius`,
`--kui-radius-sm`, `--kui-control-size`, `--kui-control-size-primary`,
`--kui-icon-size`, `--kui-font`, `--kui-font-size`, `--kui-transition`, `--kui-scrim`.

## Keyboard

`Space`/`k` play-pause · `←`/`→` ∓10s · `↑`/`↓` volume · `m` mute · `f` fullscreen ·
`i` Picture-in-Picture · `c` subtitles · `0`-`9` jump to percent · `j`/`l` ∓10s · `,`/`.` frame step (paused) ·
`<`/`>` speed · `Home`/`End` · `?` key list · `Esc` close the menu or leave emulated fullscreen.
Remap with the React prop `shortcuts={{ seekForward: 'n', captions: false }}` (`false` = none).
On the focused seek bar: `←`/`→` ∓5s, `PageUp`/`PageDown` ∓10%, `Home`/`End`.

## Touch

Single tap toggles the controls (never pauses). Double tap a side seeks. Press and hold
plays at 2×. Horizontal drag scrubs, vertical drag on the right changes volume.

## Accessibility

Everything is reachable by Tab with a visible focus ring; the chrome does not auto-hide
while a control holds keyboard focus. The seek bar is a real slider with
`aria-valuetext` ("2:14 of 4:20"). Menus and dialogs trap focus, close on `Esc` and
restore it. A polite live region announces play state, quality, subtitle and audio
changes, fullscreen, PiP, Cast and errors. Contrast meets WCAG AA;
`prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured. CI runs axe-core over four player states.

## Privacy

The player makes no request other than the media you give it, writes nothing to
`localStorage`, `sessionStorage` or cookies, and loads no fonts, icons or analytics.
Enabling Cast loads Google's sender SDK from gstatic.com — the single exception, opt-in,
and the only allowance in the CI test that enforces all of the above.

## Events

    engine.on('ready', ({ startupMs, timeToFirstFrameMs }) => …)
    engine.on('stall', ({ count, durationMs, totalMs }) => …)
    engine.on('quartile', ({ percent }) => …)          // 25 | 50 | 75 | 100
    engine.on('complete' | 'error' | 'sourcechange' | 'play' | 'pause'
             | 'seeking' | 'seeked' | 'ratechange' | 'volumechange'
             | 'qualitychange' | 'audiotrackchange', handler)

Measured locally and sent nowhere. Every subscription returns an unsubscribe
function, and a listener that throws cannot break playback.

## Chapters, storyboards, playlists, live

    <VideoPlayer chapters="/chapters.vtt" thumbnails="/storyboard.vtt" />
    <VideoPlayer playlist={[{ src, title, poster }, …]} playlistCountdown={5} />

Chapters segment the seek bar and appear in the settings menu. Storyboards
support sprite sheets through the `#xywh=` media fragment. Live streams are
detected from the source (see Live streams).

## Live streams, presence check, alternate sources

All generic: nothing knows what is streamed. Recipe: recipes/live-streams.md.

    type LiveOptions = {
      dvr?: boolean;                 // seek bar over the DVR window; default false
      stopWhenHidden?: boolean;      // default true
      reauth?: boolean | { maxAttempts?: number; baseDelayMs?: number; maxDelayMs?: number };  // 5 / 1000 / 15000
      credentials?: 'same-origin' | 'include';   // default 'same-origin'
    };
    <VideoPlayer src="…/live.m3u8" adapters={adapters} live />

- Live = the HLS playlist has no `EXT-X-ENDLIST` (the hls adapter reads `details.live` on
  every refresh; Safari: unbounded `duration`). A live stream shows a LIVE badge, "Go to live edge"
  when behind (tolerance = hls.js target latency + one segment, at least 10 s), no seek bar, no
  ±10 s buttons, no seek shortcuts, and never "ended" (a live playlist that repeats one segment
  with `EXT-X-DISCONTINUITY` is just a live playlist).
- `live` as a hint (true / object) makes `createHlsAdapter` pass `startLevel: 0` and
  `capLevelToPlayerSize: true` (override with `config`). The adapter always passes
  `liveDurationInfinity: true`.
- Reload: on 401 / 403 / 404 (a deleted path, an ended session) for a live source the adapter
  destroys the hls.js instance and loads the ORIGINAL url again at once (redirects followed,
  same-origin cookies sent), then backs off (1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... ≤ 15 s); network errors reconnect with the
  same back-off; after `maxAttempts` the error `LIVE_REFUSED` / `LIVE_UNAVAILABLE` with a Try again
  button. A segment that loads resets the count. A source never seen playing is not reopened: its
  refusal is shown at once. The refusal text (JSON `message` or short plain text) is
  `PlayerError.detail`. Safari's native HLS gives no status codes: the ordinary network retry applies.
- Stop when hidden (live only): out of the viewport (IntersectionObserver) or a hidden tab →
  the element is paused and `adapter.suspend()` runs (hls.js `stopLoad()`; native: the source is
  dropped); back in view → `adapter.resume()` (`startLoad(-1)` + jump to the live edge) and play if it
  was playing. Not while in Picture-in-Picture, AirPlay or Cast.

Presence ("Still watching?"):

    import { createPresenceGroup } from "@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player";        // also from /react
    import { PresenceGroupProvider, PresencePrompt, usePresenceGroup } from "@kuraykaraaslan/kui-player/react";

    <VideoPlayer presence={{ everyMs: 600_000, graceMs: 30_000 }} />
    <PresenceGroupProvider everyMs={600_000} graceMs={30_000}>   // or group={createPresenceGroup(...)}
      <VideoPlayer … /> × N                                       // one timer, one page-level prompt
    </PresenceGroupProvider>

`PresenceGroupProvider` props: `group?`, `everyMs?`, `graceMs?`, `prompt?` (true; false = render
`<PresencePrompt group />` yourself), `locale?`, `injectStyles?`. `PresenceGroup`: `options`, `store`
(`{ phase: 'idle' | 'watching' | 'asking', remainingMs, everyMs, graceMs }`), `join(member)`,
`update()`, `confirm()`, `dispose()`. The timer counts playback only and runs while at least one member
plays. `confirm()` (the Continue button, Esc, or a viewer pressing Play) restarts the count. With no
answer within `graceMs` every playing member pauses and stops loading; each shows "Paused to save data" +
Play. A player inside a provider uses the group's timing and prompt; `presence={false}` opts out.

Alternate sources: `sources=[{label, src}]` (+ `preferAlternateInFullscreen`, `onSourceChange`).
They take the Quality menu (values `"0"`, `"1"` ...); switching keeps position for on-demand video and
rejoins the edge for live.

Events (engine.on): `presence:ask {graceMs}`, `presence:continue`, `presence:timeout`,
`suspend {reason: 'hidden'|'presence'}`, `resume {reason}`, `live:reconnect {attempt, reason: 'auth'|'network'}`,
`live:recovered`; adapter errors now also reach `error`. New dictionary keys (all six locales):
`presenceTitle`, `presenceCountdown` (`{seconds}`), `presenceContinue`, `presencePaused`, `reconnecting`,
`error.LIVE_REFUSED`, `error.LIVE_UNAVAILABLE`, `state.reconnecting`, `state.presencePaused`.

## Subtitles

WebVTT rides on the element's own text tracks. SRT and ASS are fetched and timed
by the player, with the parser loaded alongside the file. Caption appearance —
colour, background opacity, edge style, font — is in the settings menu and in the
store.

## Persistence

    <VideoPlayer persist />
    <VideoPlayer persist={{ key: 'app', storage: sessionStorage, resume: false }} />

Off by default. Preferences (volume, speed, subtitle language and size) are
source-independent; position is per source, expires after 30 days, and is
*offered* rather than applied.

## Errors

`store.error` is a `PlayerError { code, name, message, recoverable, detail? }` mapped from
`MediaError`, plus the `<source>`-only failure browsers report on the source element.
Network errors retry automatically with backoff (500 ms / 1 s / 2 s, three attempts);
`engine.retry()` is the manual path and both restore the previous position.

## DRM

Widevine and PlayReady through hls.js (CMAF `cbcs` + HLS). `createHlsAdapter({ Hls, drm: { widevine: { licenseUrl, headers }, playready: { licenseUrl, headers } } })`.
`headers` is an async callback run for every license request (short-lived token). The DRM code is a
separate chunk loaded only when `drm` is set. Errors: `DRM_UNSUPPORTED`, `DRM_LICENSE_DENIED`
(401/403), `DRM_LICENSE_NETWORK` (retryable), `DRM_OUTPUT_RESTRICTED`. Safari/iOS (FairPlay) are not
supported and get `DRM_UNSUPPORTED` rather than a silent stall. See recipes/drm.md.
